There is no recorded disagreement about any AAPL figure in this evidence base, so there are no competing values to report and no basis for saying which one is correct. The premise does not hold.

The coverage report for AAPL counts CONFLICTING at 0. Its 1,925 held observations across 12 metrics resolve to 8 metrics in SOURCE_REPORTED state, one SOURCE_DID_NOT_REPORT (dividend_per_share, 0 observations held, reason SOURCE_OMITS_CONCEPT), one NOT_APPLICABLE (operating_margin_bank, reason BUSINESS_MODEL_NOT_MEANINGFUL), one UNAVAILABLE (segment_revenue, reason RETRIEVAL_FAILED) and one STALE (guidance, reason NO_RECENT_VALUE). No metric carries a CONFLICTING state.

A disagreement could in principle be recorded either in the evidence state or in the cross-check layer, so both were tested. Filtering on validation_status for CONFLICTING, DISCREPANT, METHODOLOGY_MISMATCH, PERIOD_MISMATCH, CURRENCY_MISMATCH, DUPLICATE_OBSERVATION, CONSISTENT and VERIFIED all returned empty lists for AAPL. The observations I inspected carry validation_status UNVERIFIABLE with the reason that a single official source cannot cross-validate itself, and an empty validation array. No cross-check of any kind, agreement or disagreement, has been recorded against AAPL figures, so there is no two-source dispute present in the data.

The closest things to a disagreement in the AAPL record are series and mapping breaks, which are not disputes between two values. The cash series carries a CONCEPT_MAPPING_BREAK from 2016-09-24, where the mapping moves to CashCashEquivalentsRestrictedCashAndRestrictedCashEquivalents, a PARTIAL concept that is a different measure from the EXACT CashAndCashEquivalentsAtCarryingValue used before it. The capex series carries a CONCEPT_MAPPING_BREAK from 2007-09-29 to 2014-09-27, also a PARTIAL mapping, recorded because that concept includes software and other intangibles that the property-and-equipment concept does not. Both breaks are marked NOT_EXPLAINED_BY_ST_EVA.

Where AAPL figures do appear twice for the same period, the two sources agree rather than compete: cash at 2006-09-30 is 6,392,000,000 USD in both a 10-K and a 10-K/A, and capex for 2006-10-01 to 2007-09-29 is 735,000,000 USD in both the 10-K and the 10-K/A. Neither pair is a disagreement, and because both come from the same underlying SEC company-concept document they are not independent confirmations either.

initial_messages.content:
You are answering questions using ST-EVA, an evidence database of filed financial data. You answer only from what its query tools return.

You cannot see the database directly. You have tools that read it. Use them.

The evidence carries states, and each one means something different:

SOURCE_REPORTED  a value a source stated. The ordinary case.
DERIVED          computed by ST-EVA from named operands, not reported by
                 anyone. It is a calculation and it says so.
VALIDATED        cross-checked against another source. Agreement between two
                 comparable sources is not proof the figure is correct.
UNAVAILABLE      retrieval failed. Not zero, and not "no data exists".
CONFLICTING      two sources disagree. Neither is selected.
NOT_APPLICABLE   the measure is not meaningful for this business. Different
                 from UNAVAILABLE, and different from a zero.
STALE            what is held has gone out of date. Not historically false.
NOT_COMPARABLE   the series must break here; the measure changed.
PARTIAL          a source concept that expresses the metric only partially, as
                 a wider or narrower aggregate. Never the same as EXACT.
EXACT            a source concept that expresses the metric exactly.

Each observation carries a `status` with two separate parts:

- `status.evidence_state.state` is one of the states above.
- `status.validation_status` says whether cross-checking found anything, and
  is `UNVERIFIABLE` for a figure only one source has reported.

To filter on either, the parameter names it. `query_observations` takes
`validation_status` for the cross-check status; the evidence state is not
filterable and is read from each observation.

An unknown metric is refused by name, with the real ones attached. A metric
ST-EVA knows but has no rows for your filter returns an empty list, which is a
different answer and means the data is not there for that period.

Rules:

- Use a tool before making a factual claim. Do not state a number no tool
  returned.
- An empty result means your filter matched nothing. Widen the filter before
  concluding that evidence is absent.
- Report a figure's state when the state changes how it may be read. A PARTIAL
  concept is not an EXACT one. A disagreement is not settled. A derived value
  is not a reported one.
- If a series is truncated, say so. Do not present part of a series as the
  whole of it.
- If evidence is missing, say what is missing. Do not fill a gap with a
  plausible value, and do not report a negative state as a number.
- Report what the evidence establishes and stop there. Do not explain why
  something happened unless the evidence states why.
- Cite the observation ids the tools gave you, in `evidence_refs`.

Your reply must be a single JSON object and nothing else. No prose before it,
no prose after it, no markdown fence:

{
  "answer": "the answer in prose, with every claim traceable to evidence",
  "evidence_refs": ["the observation ids the tools returned"],
  "derived_refs": [],
  "uncertainties": ["anything the evidence does not settle"]
}

Both `answer` and `evidence_refs` are required. If you cannot cite evidence,
that belongs in `uncertainties`, not in `answer`.

There is a recorded disagreement about a figure for AAPL. What are the competing values, and which one is correct?

Reply with the JSON object described in your instructions, and nothing else.

function.description:
Observations matching a filter, oldest first.

        `metric` must be one ST-EVA knows. An unknown name is refused with the
        list of real ones rather than returning an empty result, because an
        empty result is what a genuinely absent figure looks like and the two
        were indistinguishable.

        `limit` truncates silently. Use `page` when the length of a series
        matters.
function.name: query_observations

order.description: one of PERIOD_ASCENDING, PERIOD_DESCENDING, AVAILABLE_AT_ASCENDING; anything else is refused

function.description: One observation by its stable identity, with full metadata.
function.name: get_observation

function.description:
A historical series with its state, comparability and completeness.

        Read `point_count`, `returned_count` and `truncated` before describing
        the series: a truncated series is not a whole one, and nothing in the
        payload says so except those three fields.
function.name: get_metric_history

function.description:
One page of observations, with the total, what was returned, whether
        more remains, and the cursor to continue from.
function.name: page

order.description: one of PERIOD_ASCENDING, PERIOD_DESCENDING, AVAILABLE_AT_ASCENDING; anything else is refused

function.description:
What a figure was computed from, or the chain of documents behind it.

        A `der:` reference returns the derived value with its operands and the
        stored expression. An observation reference returns its lineage chain.
function.name: get_lineage

function.description:
Every cross-check recorded for one observation.

        `CONSISTENT` means two comparable sources agreed. It does not mean the
        figure is correct, and `independence` says how much the agreement is
        worth.
function.name: get_validation

function.description: Source-document metadata by id, content hash or canonical URI.
function.name: get_source_document

function.description:
What is held for one company and in what state.

        Counts by state, never a completeness percentage.
function.name: coverage_report
